title: Felix and the Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1918, on a storm-battered northern coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Casper Nakamura keeps his head down and his lamp lit, convinced that history is something that happens to other people. Then a stranger named Ilsa washes ashore carrying letters in the unmistakable handwriting of Casper's dead friend Anton — a forger and document-maker the war was supposed to have erased. The letters point to Anton's hidden workshop, where forged uniforms, passports, and a single unfinished document could still save lives or damn them, and where the armistice deadline gives them weeks, not months. As soldiers, smugglers, and a vengeful quartermaster close in, Casper must decide whether invisibility was ever really a choice. The novel ends with the armistice signed and the workshop burned, Ilsa gone into a new identity, and Casper keeping the lighthouse — no longer a man history happens around, but one who finally signed his own name to something.
about_author: Emrys Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in coastal municipal collections, where the gaps in the record fascinated her more than the entries. She writes from a house within sight of a decommissioned lighthouse, and Felix and the Uniform is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Lamp That Never Asks
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes the lighthouse routine, his grief for his wife Maren, and his creed that history happens elsewhere. A supply boat fails to arrive; the storm season begins early. Emotional beat: numb, orderly solitude about to be cracked open.

chapters.title: What the Sea Gave Back
chapters.summary: Casper finds Ilsa half-drowned on the shingle with a waterproof satchel she refuses to surrender. She speaks little, watches everything, and flinches at uniforms. Emotional beat: wary hospitality; two people measuring each other for threat.

chapters.title: A Hand He Buried
chapters.summary: Casper discovers letters in the satchel in Anton's handwriting — Anton, who died at the front two years ago, or so the telegram said. The letters reference a workshop and a deadline. Emotional beat: vertigo; the dead writing to the living.

chapters.title: The Quartermaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She reveals fragments: she was Anton's courier, and a quartermaster named Brandt is hunting a missing crate of forged documents. She doesn't trust Casper yet. Emotional beat: controlled fear, the cost of carrying secrets alone.

chapters.title: Twelve Miles of Bad Road
chapters.summary: Casper and Ilsa travel inland to the abandoned herring cannery where Anton's workshop hides. The village shows war's fingerprints: ration notices, a wall of photographs of the fallen. Emotional beat: dread of returning to a world Casper opted out of.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: Inside the cannery: inks, stamps, blank passports, and Anton's half-finished masterpiece — a document that could extract a condemned family across the border. A note: 'Finish it before the guns stop. After that, paper means nothing.' Emotional beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Uniforms Make the Man
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. To move freely they must become someone else; Ilsa begins teaching him forgery, and he is disturbingly good at it. Trying on a forged uniform, he glimpses how power fits like a costume. Emotional beat: seduction and self-disgust.

chapters.title: Brandt
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The quartermaster arrives in the coastal village, methodical and charming, interrogating the postmistress. He keeps a ledger of debts he intends to collect. Emotional beat: cold menace; the antagonist as an administrator of cruelty.

chapters.title: Maren's Hand
chapters.summary: Casper, practicing forged signatures, realizes his own hand has changed since Maren died — and finds one of her letters he never opened. Grief and craft entwine. Emotional beat: the chapter's quiet heart; memory as both wound and tool.

chapters.title: The Postmistress's Silence
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The postmistress, who recognized Ilsa, chooses silence but demands a favor: forged discharge papers for her son, a deserter hiding in her cellar. Emotional beat: complicity spreading; every kindness has a signature.

chapters.title: A Crate on the Night Tide
chapters.summary: Casper and Ilsa retrieve the missing crate Brandt seeks — inside, evidence that Anton faked his own death and may still be alive. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous intoxicant; Casper begins to want things again.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Dead
chapters.summary: Anton's POV (flashback interleave). How he vanished, why he let the world believe him dead, and why the final document must be finished by someone who never wanted power. Emotional beat: elegy and guilt; the mentor's absence made present.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at the Mill
chapters.summary: Carrying papers to the border contact, Casper is stopped by Brandt's men. He passes — barely — by impersonating an officer with terrifying fluency, and hates how naturally it comes. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the first taste of corruption's convenience.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Signed
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She confesses she once forged documents for Brandt before defecting, and that her real name is on his list. Trust between her and Casper fractures and re-forms. Emotional beat: confession as risk; intimacy through shared shame.

chapters.title: The Storm of the Century
chapters.summary: The great storm hits. The lamp must be kept lit or boats die on the rocks — including, possibly, the border contact's. Casper chooses the lamp over the deadline. Emotional beat: duty versus urgency; keeper's vow tested.

chapters.title: Brandt at the Door
chapters.summary: Brandt, tracing the crate, arrives at the cannery while Casper is at the lighthouse. Ilsa hides the workshop, stalls him with forged authority, and barely survives the encounter. Emotional beat: terror under poise; the mask nearly slips.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Casper returns; together they finish Anton's document in a single feverish night, Casper signing it with his own true name — the first honest signature in the book. Emotional beat: catharsis; identity chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: Armistice Eve
chapters.summary: Word spreads that the guns stop at dawn. Brandt, facing a world where his ledgers lose meaning, moves to seize the workshop and burn the evidence of his own dealings. Emotional beat: countdown dread; peace arriving too slowly.

chapters.title: Fire in the Cannery
chapters.summary: Climax. Confrontation at the workshop: Brandt versus Casper and Ilsa amid the flames. The finished document is smuggled out through the smoke; Anton's life's work burns rather than fall into Brandt's hands. Emotional beat: sacrifice, violence, and moral clarity at last.

chapters.title: The Guns Stop
chapters.summary: Armistice morning. Bells, silence, strangers weeping in the street. Casper watches the village celebrate a history he is no longer outside of. Brandt's fate is left to the new authorities — and to his own ledger of debts. Emotional beat: exhausted, unearned-feeling relief.

chapters.title: A Name on the Passenger List
chapters.summary: Ilsa departs under her new identity, the rescued family's document delivered. She and Casper part without promises, but she leaves him one of Anton's blank passports — a door, not a demand. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; love acknowledged by letting go.

chapters.title: The Keeper Signs the Log
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, months later. The lighthouse is decommissioned for winter; he writes the log in his own hand, adds Maren's name and Anton's to the record, and begins his own first letter — signed, dated, true. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; a man who finally belongs to his own history.
